And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) made clear that that caliphate is upon the pattern of prophethood, as in the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman in the Musnad of Ahmad, that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Prophethood will be among you as long as God wills it to be, then He will lift it when He wills to lift it. Then there will be a caliphate upon the pattern of prophethood as long as God wills it to be, then He will lift it when He wills to lift it. Then there will be a biting kingship as long as God wills it to be, then He will lift it when He wills to lift it. Then there will be a coercive kingship as long as God wills it to be, then He will lift it when He wills to lift it. Then there will be a caliphate upon the pattern of prophethood" — and he fell silent.

Servants of God, in our taking up that guidance we cannot be blamed for having criticised the ages that preceded us, between us and the Companions. What certain people do by way of debate and dispute, when they say that those who preceded us from the people of the last century and the one before it were upon good and are better than us, and did not do this that you are doing — this argument is flimsy, because all of us, we and the people of the last century and the people of the century before it and the people of the century before that, are all dependants of the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and followers of them; and no one can bring anything more excellent than what the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) brought. Whoever takes a model, let him take the most excellent as his model. That is no impugning of those before us and no criticism of them, for they have gone on to what they sent ahead, and our task is to seek forgiveness for them and to pray to God for them, as God praised the later ones of this community for doing.

God, Glorified and Exalted, has given glad tidings of generations to come in this community in a number of the verses of His Book. In Sūrat al-Ḥashr, after mentioning the Emigrants and the Helpers, He said: {And those who came after them say: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any rancour towards those who believed. Our Lord, You are indeed Most Kind, Most Merciful} (Sūrat al-Ḥashr 59:10). This is our state towards all who went before: of all who preceded us of our fathers and our grandfathers and the past generations we say: {Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any rancour towards those who believed. Our Lord, You are indeed Most Kind, Most Merciful}.

Among God's glad tidings of these later generations is His saying, Exalted is He, in Sūrat al-Jumuʿah: {and others of them who have not yet joined them; and He is the Mighty, the Wise} (Sūrat al-Jumuʿah 62:3). This is a glad tiding of the generation that will come: "and others of them", that is, of the followers of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him); "who have not yet joined them", that is, that they will join them — for lammā negates a past that is interrupted, meaning that this will be interrupted and they will join them. So this is a glad tiding from God, Glorified and Exalted, of later generations in this community in whom there is great good; and it is enough of an honouring of them that God, Glorified and Exalted, has promised them that they will join the first generations. "Who have not yet joined them" is an announcement that they will join them, and this is enough by way of raising their worth and rank: that they should be described as ones who will join the earlier generations of this community and the forerunners among the Emigrants and the Helpers.

Servants of God, we are in this country in the west of this Islamic community, and many hadiths have come mentioning the merit of the west of this community. Muslim recorded in the Ṣaḥīḥ that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A group of my community will not cease to be manifest upon the truth; neither those who oppose them nor those who forsake them will harm them, until the command of God comes while they are in that state — and they are the people of the west." So we must be eager to be among that group, manifest upon the truth, who are of the people of the west, until we meet God, Glorified and Exalted, having given what we pledged to God and having been true in what we promised Him, Glorified and Exalted.

And we must know that God has no need of us, and that He will make His religion mighty through the might of one who is mighty or through the abasement of one who is abased; and that if we draw back from supporting this religion, God will bring forth from the generations those who will support it and who will not fear the blame of any blamer, as God Most High said: {O you who believe, whoever of you turns back from his religion, God will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble towards the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, striving in the path of God and not fearing the blame of any blamer. That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills; and God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing} (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:54).

May God bless me and you in the Mighty Qur'an, and may He benefit me and you by the verses and the wise remembrance that are in it. And may He turn in forgiveness to me and to you; indeed He is the Ever-Relenting, the Most Merciful.

flags.arabic: إن رجلا من أبناء المسلمين وقف في ملإ وناد عظيم من الناس في الأسبوع الماضي … تبا له كيف يقارن أحدا برسول الله (ص)
flags.context: Near the end of the sermon, on the manifestations of the Jahiliyyah surviving today.
options: Translate in full and faithfully, as done here
flags.note: Contemporary political criticism. The Sheikh reports an unnamed man, at an unnamed public gathering, comparing an unnamed head of state favourably with the Prophet, calls down perdition on him (تبا له), calls the leader 'a tyrant among the tyrants of this world', and says the whole assembly was competing 'in the arena of hypocrisy'. Neither the man, the leader nor the state is identified in the Arabic, and nothing has been added to identify them. The passage is translated neither softened nor strengthened; whether and how to publish it in English is for Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office to decide.

flags.context: لا تزال طائفة من أمتي ظاهرين على الحق … وهم أهل الغرب — followed by the Sheikh applying it to 'this country, in the west of this Islamic community'.
options: and they are the people of the west (the Sheikh's reading, applied to the Muslim west)
and they are the people of Damascus / al-Gharb, a place name
and they are the people of the large water-bucket (al-gharb), i.e. those who draw water
flags.note: The closing phrase of this narration is classically disputed, and at least three readings of 'ahl al-gharb' are current. The Sheikh takes the geographical reading and applies it to Mauritania; the English follows his reading because his application depends on it, but a reviewer should know the phrase is contested and that no alternative is discussed in the text.

flags.context: On circumambulating the Kaaba naked in the Jahiliyyah.
options: the Hums (al-Ḥums), transliterated and left unglossed as here
a short gloss such as 'the Quraysh ritual confederacy'
flags.note: al-Ḥums is a pre-Islamic ritual grouping of Quraysh and their allies, who claimed exemptions in the pilgrimage rites. The Sheikh gives no gloss, and none has been added; the term is unknown to most English readers and is a candidate for the corpus glossary rather than an in-text expansion.

flags.arabic: وا صباحاه يا آل عبد مناف
flags.context: The Prophet's cry from al-Safa when he was permitted to proclaim the call openly.
options: Alarm! A raid at daybreak! (rendering the sense of the cry)
flags.note: Wā ṣabāḥāh is the conventional Arabian cry raising the alarm at a dawn raid; its force in the passage depends on the hearers recognising it as such, which is why the sense has been rendered rather than the words. The expansion is editorial and is marked here.

flags.arabic: صحبوا العوذ المطافيل   /   أُشابة من الناس
flags.context: The speech of Urwah ibn Mas'ud at al-Hudaybiyah.
options: have brought out their milch-camels with their young / a motley of people
have brought out their women and children / a mixed rabble
flags.note: Both phrases are idiomatic. al-ʿūdh al-maṭāfīl are she-camels newly delivered with their young at foot, and the idiom conventionally signals that Quraysh had come out with their families, meaning they would not retreat; ushābah is a mixed, ill-assorted crowd. The literal rendering has been kept and the idiomatic sense noted here rather than resolved in the text.

flags.arabic: واذكروا إذ أنتم قليل مستضعفون في الأرض، تخافون أن يتخطفكم الناس   /   يسبشرون بنعمة من الله
flags.context: Two Qur'anic quotations in the second half of the sermon.
options: Mark the first as a quotation and correct nothing in the Arabic, as done here
flags.note: Two source defects in quoted scripture. The first (Q 8:26) is run into the prose without the ornate brackets used everywhere else on this page. The second, within Q 3:171, reads يسبشرون for يستبشرون — a dropped letter. Both are preserved in body_ar and neither has been silently repaired.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.

This is a sermon, not a fatwa: it contains no legal rulings, and its closing formula ('May God bless me and you in the Mighty Qur'an') is the standard end of the first part of a Friday sermon. The site classifies it under written da'wah material.
Lines of verse are rendered as prose in italics, per house style; the source marks hemistich breaks with a double asterisk.
Unlike several neighbouring records in this range, the Qur'anic quotations here are present and marked with ornate brackets in the Arabic. Two exceptions are noted in the flags.
